lesson.subject: maths
lesson.title: Telling the Time to Five Minutes
lesson.summary: Read and write the time to five minutes, past and to the hour, on an analogue clock.
lesson.unit: Topic 11: Telling the time to five minutes
learning_objectives: Count in fives round the clock
Tell the time five minutes past and to

standards.text: Tell and write the time to five minutes, including quarter past/to the hour, and draw the hands on a clock face; know the number of minutes in an hour and hours in a day

success_criteria: I can count in fives round the clock
I can read times like 10 past 7 and 10 to 4
I can say which time takes longer
lesson.real_life: Knowing when the school bus comes, when lessons start and how long a break lasts.

warm_up.prompt: How many minutes in half an hour?
The clock shows o'clock when the long hand is on the 12.

blocks.alt: A small round alarm clock with numbers 1 to 12 on a dark table
blocks.caption: An alarm clock with a long and a short hand.
blocks.credit: Photo by Suhas Hanjar on Unsplash
blocks.say: Meet Zara. She has a big wall clock in her classroom. The clock tells her when to learn and when to play. Let's learn to read it.

blocks.markdown:
A **minute** is a short time. 60 minutes make 1 **hour**.

24 hours make 1 day and night.
blocks.say: A minute is a short time. An hour is longer. There are sixty minutes in one hour. There are twenty-four hours in one whole day.

scenes.caption: Minute hand: one trip = 60 minutes.
scenes.say: The long hand is the minute hand. It goes round the clock in one hour.
It stops at each number. Each number is five minutes. Count with me: five, ten, fifteen.
At the six, it is thirty minutes. All the way round is sixty!

blocks.alt: A clock face with the five-minute numbers 5 to 60 outside the hour numbers
blocks.caption: Count in fives round the clock.
blocks.say: The big numbers count in fives. The minute hand points at them.

question.prompt: How many minutes are in 1 hour?

blocks.markdown:
The short **hour hand** shows the hour.

The long **minute hand** shows the minutes. Count in fives.
blocks.say: The short hand is the hour hand. It tells us the hour. The long hand tells us the minutes. Count in fives to read it.

scenes.caption: 12 = o'clock.
scenes.say: Start at the twelve. Zero minutes. That is o'clock.

scenes.caption: 1 = 5 past, 2 = 10 past.
scenes.say: Move to the one. Five minutes past. Move to the two. Ten minutes past.
At the three it is fifteen. At the six it is thirty. That is half past.

question.prompt: Count in fives: 5, 10, 15, what comes next?

blocks.title: Zara follows the minute hand
blocks.transcript: It is five o'clock. Zara wakes up for Fajr. The minute hand points to the twelve. That is o'clock. It hops round in fives. Five, ten, fifteen. Later it is half past seven. The bus is here! Now the hand is on the ten. It is ten to eight. Two more hops. Eight o'clock. School starts! At quarter past three, school ends. Sixty minutes in an hour. Twenty-four hours in a day. Well done, Zara!
blocks.caption: Zara counts the clock in fives through her day.

points: Each number on the clock is 5 more minutes
blocks.say: Remember. Sixty minutes in an hour. Twenty-four hours in a day. Count round the clock in fives.

terms.meaning: A short time. There are 60 in an hour.
The short hand. It shows the hour.
The long hand. It shows the minutes.

blocks.markdown:
**Past** means minutes after the hour, up to half past.

10 past 7 is 7:10.
blocks.say: The first half of the hour uses the word past. The hand has gone past the hour. Zara's bus comes at ten past seven.

scenes.caption: Hour hand just past 7.
scenes.say: The hour hand is just after the seven.

scenes.say: The minute hand is on the two. Two fives make ten minutes.

scenes.caption: 10 past 7 = 7:10.
scenes.say: Ten minutes past seven. We write it as seven ten.

blocks.markdown:
20 past 4 is 4:20.

Hour hand just after 4, minute hand on 4.
blocks.say: Now set the clock. For twenty past four, put the minute hand on the four. Then the hour hand sits just after four.

scenes.caption: 4 fives = 20.
scenes.say: Twenty minutes. Count in fives: five, ten, fifteen, twenty.

scenes.caption: Hour hand just past 4.
scenes.say: Put the long hand on the four. The short hand moves a little past the four.

blocks.title: Make a paper clock
materials: Two paper strips for the hands
instructions: Make a long minute hand and a short hour hand.

question.prompt: What is the time when the minute hand is on 2 and the hour hand is just past 6?
question.hint: Hour hand first, then count the minutes.
question.explanation: 2 is 10 minutes. The hour is 6. So 10 past 6.

points: Number on the clock times 5 = minutes
The hour hand sits just past the hour
blocks.say: Remember. Minute hand on the number times five. Past means after the hour. Hour hand sits just after the hour.

blocks.markdown:
**To** means minutes before the next hour.

10 to 4 is 3:50.
blocks.say: After half past, the minute hand goes up the right side. Now we count how many minutes are left to the next hour. We say to.

scenes.caption: 10 on the clock = 50 minutes.
scenes.say: The minute hand is on the ten. That is fifty minutes past three.

scenes.caption: 10 minutes left.
scenes.say: How far to the twelve? Two fives. Ten minutes left!

scenes.caption: 10 to 4 = 3:50.
scenes.say: So it is ten to four. The next hour is four.

question.prompt: The minute hand is on the 11. How many minutes to the next hour?
question.explanation: 11 is 55 minutes, so 5 minutes to the hour.

blocks.text: Stop 2: What time will it be?

blocks.markdown:
Past is before half past. To is after half past.

10 to 9 plus 10 minutes is 9 o'clock.
blocks.say: Race time! It is ten to nine. What time will it be in ten minutes? Hop on the minute hand to the twelve.

scenes.say: Ten to nine. The minute hand is on the ten.

scenes.caption: + 10 minutes.
scenes.say: Hop two fives. Five, then ten. The hand is on the twelve!

blocks.title: Clock match
blocks.say: Flip the cards and find the matching pairs. A little brain break!

question.prompt: It is 5 to 6. What time will it be in 5 minutes?

points: To: minutes left to the next hour
blocks.say: Remember. Past is after the hour. To is before the next hour. Use the next hour for to.

blocks.markdown:
A **quarter hour** is 15 minutes. A **half hour** is 30 minutes.

Times of the day go in order.
blocks.say: Zara wakes for Fajr at five o'clock. The bus comes at half past seven. School starts at eight. Home time is quarter past three.

question.prompt: Which time is earlier in the day: 7:30 or 3:15 in the afternoon?

blocks.markdown:
An **interval** is the time between two times.

9:00 to 10:00 is 1 hour.
blocks.say: How long is a lesson? Maths starts at nine and ends at ten. One hour passes. We call the time between two times an interval.

scenes.caption: 9:00 start.
scenes.say: Maths starts at nine o'clock.

scenes.caption: 10:00 end.
scenes.say: It ends at ten o'clock. The minute hand went round once.

scenes.caption: 1 hour = 60 minutes.
scenes.say: One hour! Sixty minutes in the lesson.

blocks.answer_markdown: 45 minutes. Half an hour is only 30 minutes.

blocks.say: Remember. Put the day in order. Compare how long things take. Use quarter hour and half hour.
